- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to underpredict early spikes; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for the first 5–7 days after sentiment shift.
- Model consistently overestimates 30-day mean by 2–5% in bullish sentiment periods; apply downward bias of 2–3% to 30d average if sentiment >0.25.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots by 3–8% in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.20) for 5+ consecutive days, model underestimates mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast for 7–10 days.
- Model frequently lags 1–3 days in response to sentiment shifts; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment changes >0.10 in 3-day window.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows >10% deviation from 14d moving average, adjust forecast to align with 14d MA unless sentiment strongly bullish (then allow 5% deviation).
